syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

book.title: Ganita Prakash Part-II
book.edition: NCERT (reprint year not stated in the prelims)

concepts.learning_objective: Express a fraction or decimal as a percentage by finding an equivalent fraction with denominator 100 or multiplying by 100.
Express a percentage z% as the fraction z/100 and its equivalent forms.
Explain why expressing quantities as parts per hundred makes comparison of proportions easier.
Find a given percentage of a quantity using fraction, decimal or proportional reasoning.
Compute percentages mentally by combining easy percentages such as 10%, 5% and 20%.
Convert a ratio of parts into a fraction of the whole and then into a percentage.

topics.title: Finding the Whole and Percentages Greater than 100

concepts.learning_objective: Find the whole quantity or the remaining part when a percentage of it is known.
Interpret percentages greater than 100 as more than the whole and relate them to decimals and multiples.
Use percentages to compare proportions when the wholes are different.
Calculate percentage increase or decrease with respect to the original amount.
Calculate profit or loss percentage with respect to the cost price, and find cost or selling price from it.
Find the selling price after a percentage discount on the marked price.
Find the final price of an item when a tax such as GST is added as a percentage.
Find the amount after t years without compounding using p(1 + rt).
Find the amount after t years with compounding using p(1 + r)^t.
Find the value of a quantity that decreases by a fixed percentage over one or more periods.
Recognise that successive percentage changes compound and do not simply add.
Distinguish between comparing percentages and comparing absolute amounts.
Explain why the square drawn on the diagonal of a given square has double its area.
Construct a square of half the area of a given square and explain why halving the side does not halve the area.

topics.title: Hypotenuse of an isosceles right triangle

concepts.learning_objective: Use the relation c^2 = 2a^2 to find the hypotenuse of an isosceles right triangle.
Find the equal sides of an isosceles right triangle when its hypotenuse is known.

topics.title: The number root 2: bounds and decimal nature

concepts.learning_objective: Find successively closer decimal bounds for root 2 by squaring trial values.
Explain why root 2 is neither a terminating decimal nor a fraction m/n.
Describe Baudhayana's method of combining two different squares into one square.
State the Baudhayana-Pythagoras theorem a^2 + b^2 = c^2 for a right triangle.
Use the theorem to find a missing side of a right triangle.
Check whether a triple of positive integers is a Baudhayana triple.
Distinguish primitive Baudhayana triples from their scaled versions.
Generate Baudhayana triples using (n - 1)^2 + (2n - 1) = n^2 when 2n - 1 is a square.

topics.title: A long-standing open problem: Fermat's Last Theorem

concepts.learning_objective: State Fermat's Last Theorem and recognise which equations it rules out.
Recall the history of Fermat's Last Theorem and its proof by Andrew Wiles.
Form and solve an equation from a word problem such as the lotus problem of the Lilavati.
Find the diagonal of a square or a rectangle using the theorem.
Apply the theorem to find the side of a rhombus or the height and area of an equilateral triangle.
Check whether two ratios are proportional using cross-multiplication.
Find a missing term so that two ratios are proportional.
Explain what the representative fraction (RF) on a map shows.
Convert between map distance and geographical distance using a map ratio.

topics.title: Ratios with more than two terms

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret a ratio with more than two terms and state when two such ratios are proportional.
Scale every term of a multi-term ratio by the same factor to keep a mixture the same.

topics.title: Dividing a whole in a given ratio

concepts.learning_objective: Divide a quantity in a ratio with two or more terms using x × a / (a + b + c + ...).
Find triangle angles from a ratio and decide whether sides in a ratio can form a triangle.

topics.title: A slice of the pie: pie charts

concepts.learning_objective: Calculate the central angle of each sector of a pie chart by dividing 360° in the data's ratio.
Read quantities from the sector angles of a pie chart.
Distinguish pairs of quantities in inverse proportion from those in direct proportion.
Use the relation xy = k for quantities in inverse proportion.

topics.title: Solving inverse proportion and work problems

concepts.learning_objective: Solve word problems on workers, provisions and arrangements using inverse proportion.
Find the time taken when two agents work together by adding their work per hour.

topics.title: Fractals in nature, the Sierpinski Carpet and fractals in art

concepts.learning_objective: Explain that a fractal is a self-similar shape showing the same pattern at smaller and smaller scales, in nature and in art.
Find the number of remaining squares, holes and the remaining area at any step of the Sierpinski Carpet.
Describe the construction of the Sierpinski Triangle and count its triangles, holes and remaining area.
Find the number of sides and the perimeter at the nth step of the Koch Snowflake.
Mentally cut and rearrange simple plane shapes without drawing them.
Identify solids that have given profiles from different viewpoints.

topics.title: Faces, edges and vertices; prisms, pyramids and nets

concepts.learning_objective: Count the faces, edges and vertices of prisms and pyramids, including n-sided ones.
Recognise and reason about nets of cubes, tetrahedrons, cylinders, cones and other solids.
Find the shortest path between two points on the surface of a cuboid by drawing a suitable net and using the Baudhayana Theorem.
Define the projection of a point on a plane and compare the length of a line with its projection.
Identify the front, top and side views of a solid as projections on the vertical, horizontal and side planes.
Relate shadows in sunlight to projections and use the fact that parallel lines project to parallel lines.

topics.title: Isometric projections and drawing on isometric grids

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the isometric projection of a cube and why its edges project to equal lengths.
Draw solids made of cubes on an isometric grid using the length, depth and height axes.

topics.title: The Balancing Act: Mean as the Centre

concepts.learning_objective: Show that the mean is the value where the total distance to the lower values equals the total distance to the higher values.
Predict whether including or removing values raises, lowers or keeps the mean.

topics.title: Relatively Unchanged: Adding to or Multiplying Every Value

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why adding or subtracting a fixed number from every value shifts the mean by the same number.
Explain why multiplying every value by a fixed number multiplies the mean by that number.
Find the median as the middle value of sorted data, or the average of the two middle values.
Reason about how including or removing values changes the median.

topics.title: Finding the Unknown and Mean and Median with Frequencies

concepts.learning_objective: Use mean = sum / number of values to find a total or a missing value.
Correct a mean when one recorded value was wrong, without the full data.
Find the mean and median of data given as values with frequencies.
Name cells and ranges of a spreadsheet using column letters and row numbers.
Write SUM and AVERAGE formulae over a row or column range.
Read values, trends and changes from a line graph.
Explain when a line graph is a better choice than a column graph.

topics.title: Infographics, Activity Strips and Data Stories

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret an infographic that uses a colour scale to compare states.
Read and make a time strip of 48 half-hour boxes for a day's activities.
Interpret the trend of typical sleep duration across ages from a line graph.

topics.title: Thinking about 'Think of a Number' tricks

concepts.learning_objective: Use letter-numbers to explain why a 'Think of a Number' trick always gives the same result.
Decode a chosen date from the final answer of a multi-step trick using an algebraic expression.
Fill missing entries of a number pyramid by forming and solving equations.
Express the top of a number pyramid in terms of its bottom row.
Use algebra to find the numbers in a calendar grid from their sum.
Find the values of shapes in an algebra grid from row sums.
Arrange three digits as a 2-digit by 1-digit product to make it as large as possible.
Justify the largest-product rule by expanding products in place-value form.
Explain using algebra why sums and differences of reversed 2-digit numbers have fixed divisors.
Justify divisibility patterns of 3-digit numbers formed by cycling or repeating digits.

topics.title: Solving puzzles and word problems with algebra

concepts.learning_objective: Model age, animal and cost problems with equations and solve them.
Solve doubling-and-giving puzzles by forming an equation or working backwards.

topics.title: Rectangles, squares and why perimeter is not area

concepts.learning_objective: Find the area of a rectangle and of the triangles cut off by its diagonal using length x width.
Explain with examples why perimeter cannot be used as a measure of area.
Find the area of a path around or across a rectangular plot by subtracting or adding rectangles.

topics.title: Area of a triangle
topics.ncert_sections: Triangles; Some Applications of the Area Formula

concepts.learning_objective: Use area of a triangle = 1/2 x base x height for any triangle.
Find an unknown altitude by writing the area of a triangle with two different base-height pairs.
Use the fact that a line from a vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side halves the area of a triangle.

topics.title: Triangles between parallel lines with a common base
topics.ncert_sections: Triangles between Parallel Lines with a Common Base

concepts.learning_objective: Recognise that triangles on the same base between the same parallels have equal areas.
Use reflection in a line to find the triangle of least perimeter on a given base.
Find the area of a polygon by dividing it into triangles.
Find the area of a quadrilateral from a diagonal and the perpendiculars dropped on it.
Use area of a parallelogram = base x corresponding height.
Explain how a parallelogram is dissected into a rectangle of equal area.
Use area of a rhombus = 1/2 x product of its diagonals.

topics.title: Trapezium
topics.ncert_sections: Trapezium; Finding the Area Using Two Copies of the Trapezium

concepts.learning_objective: Use area of a trapezium = 1/2 x height x sum of the parallel sides.
Explain how two copies of a trapezium form a parallelogram and give the area formula.
Convert between units of length and area such as in, cm, ft, in2 and cm2.
Compute and estimate areas of everyday objects such as an A4 sheet.
